alerts.headline: Flood Advisory issued September 17 at 7:02PM HST until September 17 at 8:15PM HST by NWS Honolulu HI
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...The island of Hawaii in Hawaii County...

* WHEN...Until 815 PM HST.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding on roads, poor drainage areas, and in
streams. Some low-water crossings may become impassable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 656 PM HST, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges continue
to indicate heavy rain over North Hilo, South Hilo, and Puna
Districts of the Big Island. Local stream gauges upstream of Hilo
have shown rather rapid rises over the past hour at Honolii
Stream and Wailuku River. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly in the advisory area. Rain was falling at a rate
of 1 to 3 inches per hour.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Hilo, Hawaiian Paradise Park, Volcano, Glenwood, Mountain View,
Hawaii Volcanoes National Park, Hawaiian Acres, Keaau,
Orchidlands Estates, Papaikou and Pepeekeo.
alerts.instruction:
Stay away from streams, drainage ditches and low lying areas prone to
flooding.

alerts.headline: Flood Watch issued September 17 at 5:40PM HST until September 18 at 6:00AM HST by NWS Honolulu HI
alerts.description:
Remnant moisture from former Tropical Storm Norbert will bring
periods of moderate to heavy showers to mainly windward sides of the
Hawaiian Islands through late tonight.

* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Kauai, Niihau and Oahu.

* WHEN...Through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Flood prone roads and other low lying areas may be closed
due to elevated runoff and overflowing streams. Urban areas may
receive more significant flooding and property damage due to rapid
runoff.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A band of remnant moisture from Norbert will move west across the
islands through Friday, bringing moderate to locally heavy
showers to mainly windward sides of the islands. There is a
slight chance of thunderstorms as well, which could produce
briefly higher rain rates, increasing the risk of flash flooding.
alerts.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
200 PM HST Thu Sep 17 2026

For the central North Pacific...between 140W and 180W:

Western East Pacific (EP98):
Showers and thunderstorms associated with a broad area of low
pressure located well west-southwest of the southern tip of the Baja
California Peninsula remain disorganized. Environmental conditions
appear conducive for additional development of this system, and a
tropical depression is likely to form this weekend as it moves
westward at 10 to 15 mph across the western part of the East Pacific
and into the central Pacific basin.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...medium...40 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...80 percent.

Well East-Southeast of the Hawaiian Islands (Former TD15-E):
Showers and thunderstorms continue in association with the remnants
of Tropical Depression Fifteen-E. Environmental conditions appear
only marginally conducive for some development of this system as it
moves gradually westward, remaining east-southeast of the Hawaiian
Islands.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...10 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...20 percent.

$$
Forecaster Pierce/Evans/Gibbs
